judged_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse fabricates the literal string "refresh_token" as the refresh token whenever the parsed data lacks one, and in sharing mode the broken minimum schema always strips the real refresh_token, so the junk placeholder is always substituted. Callers that persist the parsed data overwrite the user's real refresh token in the DB with the placeholder string "refresh_token" — the credential is permanently destroyed (next refresh sends refresh_token=refresh_token to the provider and fails), and re-auth is the only recovery; the destruction is silent because the parse itself succeeds.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, when sharing mode is enabled it validates with `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, which does not include `refresh_token` and (as a plain `z.object(...)` without `.passthrough()`) will strip unknown keys like a real `refresh_token` from the provider response. The function then unconditionally fills a missing token with the literal string `"refresh_token"` (`if (!refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token) { refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"; }`). Callers then merge/persist this parsed data (e.g. Office365: `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }` followed by DB update), which can overwrite the real stored refresh token with the placeholder, breaking future refreshes and requiring re-auth. This destructive behavior is directly implied by the diff.
